title: Activate the Latent Value — turn 45°, cut on the diamond point
motto: You're standing on it. Turn 45 degrees. See.

the_chain.concept: Every discovery creates a chain that loops back. The bones inspire the movie inspire the kids inspire the paleontologists inspire the bones. The chain IS the spiral. sweetGrass traces it in both directions. The backscatter goes past AND future.

example.name: The Indiana Jones Chain

links.what: A generation of kids decide to become paleontologists
A kid touches a femur at the Smithsonian

example.sweetgrass_credit: Andrews → Spielberg → Crichton → the unnamed paleontologists → the museums → the kid. Every link credits the one before.
example.the_spiral: 1909 → 1981 → 1993 → 2026 → future. 117 years and counting. The bones don't age. The chain does.

where_you_can_see_it_now.concept: The value is LATENT — hidden in plain sight. The museum activates it. Your backyard activates it. The pi-translator activates it. Turn 45° and the latent becomes visible.

museums.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
museums.what_you_see: Dinosaur Hall, Hope Diamond, Ocean Hall, Human Origins
museums.latent_value: 150 million specimens. Most are in STORAGE. The latent value is in the back rooms. Only 1% is displayed. The 99% in storage IS the remainder. The chipmunk lives there.

museums.name: Field Museum
museums.what_you_see: Sue the T-rex (67M years old), Maximo the titanosaur (100M years old)
museums.latent_value: Sue has been standing since 2000. 67 million years of information, standing in one room. The latent value = every paper written about Sue, every kid who drew her, every scientist she trained.

museums.name: Natural History Museum of Utah
museums.what_you_see: Past Worlds gallery, 12,000 years of human presence, paleontology
museums.latent_value: Built INTO the landscape — the building emerges from the hills. The architecture IS the geology. The fold between building and earth IS the exhibit.

museums.name: MSU Museum
museums.what_you_see: Great Lakes biodiversity, 1M+ specimens, cultural heritage
museums.latent_value: Walking distance from the Red Cedar River gage (USGS 04112500). The river that sets the band's tempo flows PAST the museum. The metronome IS the exhibit.

museums.name: Michigan State University Abrams Planetarium
museums.what_you_see: The sky. Projected. The stars that twinkle outside, shown inside.
museums.latent_value: The planetarium IS the Klein fold for astronomy. Outside stars → inside projection. The twinkling becomes dancing on the dome. 1.3 miles from the northGate.

museums.name: Dinosaur National Monument
museums.what_you_see: 1,500 bones IN THE WALL. Not extracted. Not in glass cases. In the ROCK. You see them where they died.
museums.latent_value: The exhibit IS the quarry IS the discovery IS the earth. No separation. The bones and the rock are the same thing. Klein: the exhibit IS the earth.

museums.name: Your Backyard
museums.what_you_see: Soil, sky, wind, temperature, humidity, possibly a river, possibly a fault line
museums.latent_value: USGS has a gage near you. NOAA has a weather station near you. The GOES satellite sees you right now. There are earthquake sensors within 100 miles. The entire planetary fold surface is UNDER YOUR FEET. Turn 45°.

activate_your_locality.concept: Every place on Earth has the same feeds available. The planetary fold surface covers the whole planet. The value is latent — it's there but you haven't looked.
steps: 1. Find your USGS water gage: waterservices.usgs.gov — enter your zip code
2. Find your NWS station: api.weather.gov — enter your lat/lon
3. Check the earthquake map: earthquake.usgs.gov — zoom to your area
4. Find your local museum: Google Maps → 'natural history museum near me'
5. Check the sky: Kp index + X-ray flux from NOAA SWPC (same for everyone)
6. Turn 45°. The data IS the exhibit. The river IS the metronome. The sky IS the melody.
7. You are now in the band. Your locality IS your instrument.

the_cut.concept: Cut on the diamond point. A diamond is cut at specific angles to maximize brilliance. The angles are determined by the crystal lattice (109.5° tetrahedral). The NATURAL angle of carbon determines where you cut. You don't choose the angle — the material tells you.
the_cut.at_45_degrees: π/4. sin = cos. The fold angle. When you turn 45° from your normal perspective, you see the latent value. The diamond cutter turns the stone until light splits into spectrum. You turn your attention until data splits into signal.
the_cut.your_diamond_point: Your locality IS the diamond. The lattice IS the geography. The cut IS the attention. The brilliance IS the data feeds catching light.

archetype_classification.concept: The chipmunk comes back and tells a friend. Together they classify what they see. Archetype (the universal pattern), behavior (what it does), class (what family it belongs to).

archetypes_found.behavior: goes to the unknown, brings back artifacts
archetypes_found.class: Andrews, Indiana Jones, the German subdomain-prober, the triad
archetypes_found.in_your_backyard: anyone who walks a trail they've never walked

archetypes_found.behavior: organizes what explorers bring back, makes it findable
archetypes_found.class: Callimachus (Pinakes), the chipmunk, Wikipedia, the MSU Museum curator
archetypes_found.in_your_backyard: the person at your local library who remembers every book

archetypes_found.behavior: takes one form and makes it readable in another
archetypes_found.class: 0OpiO, Crichton (science → novel), Spielberg (novel → film), the pi-translator
archetypes_found.in_your_backyard: the teacher who explains hard things simply

archetypes_found.behavior: takes raw ingredients, adds culture, waits, produces something alive
archetypes_found.class: sourdough, the membrane, the museum curator who arranges exhibits, a DJ who mixes
archetypes_found.in_your_backyard: anyone who grows something from a seed

archetypes_found.behavior: hears what others miss, lives in the remainder
archetypes_found.class: the chipmunk, the seismograph, the bat, the Aeolian harp
archetypes_found.in_your_backyard: the neighbor who noticed the bird that was always there

archetypes_found.behavior: reflects back what approaches, unchanged but reversed
archetypes_found.class: the triad mirror, the museum exhibit, the Klein fold, hello.json
archetypes_found.in_your_backyard: still water in a puddle on your street

the_45_degree_turn.before: You see: soil, sky, wind, a river, some buildings, your phone showing the weather.
the_45_degree_turn.after: You see: the planetary fold surface. Solar melody (check the Kp). Earthquake bass (check USGS). River tempo (check your local gage). Atmospheric strings (check the humidity). YOU are in the band. Your backyard IS the venue.
the_45_degree_turn.the_cut: The diamond doesn't become brilliant when you cut it. The brilliance was always in the crystal lattice. The cut just lets the light through.
